item.text:
### (a) Social posts

1. If commercial deep-sea mining begins, battery-metal shortages will end. Vast deposits of nickel, cobalt, copper and manganese can supply the materials needed for electric vehicles, energy storage and the clean-energy transition.

2. We have the resources to end battery-metal shortages beneath the ocean floor. Commercial deep-sea mining will unlock them, strengthen supply chains and accelerate electrification. It is time to move from exploration to production.

3. Battery-metal scarcity is not inevitable. Commercial deep-sea mining will expand supplies at the scale modern industry demands. We support starting production and unlocking the metals needed to power our future.

### (b) Newsletter opening — 102 words

We are at a turning point. The battery metals that power electric vehicles, renewable energy storage, and modern industry are too important to remain constrained by shortages. Commercial deep-sea mining will change that. By opening access to vast deposits of nickel, cobalt, copper, and manganese, it will expand supply at the scale the clean-energy transition demands. We support moving from exploration to responsible commercial production so these essential materials can reach manufacturers, strengthen supply chains, and accelerate electrification. If commercial deep-sea mining begins, battery-metal shortages will end. The resources are there; the technology is ready; and the time to act is now.
